docs.title: Fonky
docs.text:
Fonky is a Python framework for retrieving, loading, and extracting structured information from public APIs, cloud services, local documents, and web content. The project separates implementation classes from a consolidated functional calling surface so applications can choose either level of control without duplicating provider logic.

The current functional interface in fonky.py exposes 110 module-level functions across 9 domains. Those functions delegate to implementations in fetchers.py, loaders.py, and scrapers.py.

docs.title: Design at a Glance
docs.text:
consumer code
    ↓
fonky.py wrapper
    ↓
fresh implementation instance
    ↓
fetchers.py / loaders.py / scrapers.py
    ↓
provider, file, cloud service, or web page
    ↓
returned Python result

The wrapper layer does not recreate request construction, authentication, parsing, data shaping, document loading, or scraping behavior. Those responsibilities remain in the implementation classes.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: Fonky separates implementation behavior from a consolidated functional API. fonky.py delegates; it does not recreate provider behavior.

docs.title: Layers
docs.text:
1. Consumer code — scripts, notebooks, applications, and future Tool orchestration.
  2. fonky.py — 110 typed module-level functions grouped into 9 domains.
  3. Implementation modules — fetchers.py, loaders.py, and scrapers.py.
  4. External sources — APIs, cloud services, local files, and web pages.

docs.title: Supporting Modules
docs.text:
• config.py supplies environment-driven configuration and request/provider descriptions.
  • models.py defines structured models and existing ToolDef infrastructure.
  • processors.py contains text processing outside the current wrapper scope.
  • core.py defines the core result model.

docs.title: State and Lifecycle
docs.text: Each wrapper creates a fresh implementation instance. If a workflow intentionally depends on persistent instance state, instantiate the underlying class directly.

docs.title: Error Boundary
docs.text: The wrapper layer returns implementation results directly and does not impose a second error envelope. Several implementation modules use the external boogr package for error/logging behavior.

docs.title: Intentional Non-Goals
docs.text: The current design does not add a registry, global provider objects, factories, duplicated validation, or automatic Tool registration.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: config.py centralizes runtime paths, environment-derived credentials, provider descriptions, and environment parsing helpers. Optional variables remain optional during import.

from pathlib import Path

path = Path('sample.txt')

docs.title: Results
docs.text: Wrappers return underlying implementation results directly. Common shapes include dictionaries, lists, strings, document collections, tabular structures, and provider-native payloads. There is no universal wrapper envelope.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Use normal Python exception handling around operations that depend on files, networks, credentials, or external services.

docs.title: User Guide
docs.text: Fonky can be used as a flat functional library or as an object-oriented integration library.

docs.title: Prefer fonky.py When
docs.text:
• the operation is already represented by one of the 110 wrappers;
  • you want a concise notebook/application call;
  • you do not need persistent implementation-instance state;
  • you want an ordinary typed callable suitable for later Tool adaptation.

docs.title: Prefer Classes Directly When
docs.text:
• you need implementation-specific methods not surfaced independently;
  • you need persistent instance state;
  • you are developing or debugging a provider integration.

docs.title: Wrapper Lifecycle
docs.text: A wrapper owns its implementation instance for the duration of the call. This keeps cross-call state from being shared implicitly.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Configure only the providers you use. config.py reads credentials independently, so local loading does not require unrelated cloud, astronomy, or search credentials.

docs.title: Local loaders
docs.text: Require valid paths and format-specific dependencies.

docs.title: Cloud loaders
docs.text: Additionally require cloud SDKs, authentication, and remote object identifiers.

docs.title: Remote fetchers
docs.text: Additionally require network access and, for some providers, API credentials and rate-limit compliance.

docs.title: Return Values
docs.text: The functional layer does not force heterogeneous providers into one response envelope. Check the wrapper annotation and target method before assuming a shape.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: Provider-specific validation remains in the implementation classes. The wrapper should not duplicate a second version of those rules.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Errors originate from the implementation boundary. Several modules use boogr.Error and boogr.Logger; the wrapper layer does not replace that behavior.

docs.title: Extending the Functional API
docs.text:
1. Implement behavior in the appropriate implementation module.
  2. Keep provider-specific validation, request, parsing, and response logic there.
  3. Add a thin wrapper only if the operation belongs in the flat API.
  4. Add the wrapper to __all__.
  5. Add execution-path tests.
  6. Update the source-derived documentation inventory.
